issue.title: test_plugins_pane_update_unknown_toasts times out in WaitForScreenTimeout at AcePage startup under the loaded full lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
Load-sensitive Textual pilot startup wait in
tests/ace/tui/test_plugins_browser_pane_update.py; see the flake report.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Found while verifying an unrelated change (a pure test-file split of
tests/test_stale_running_cleanup.py into three files; no src/ or TUI code touched).
`sase tool run check` (ToolRun 2dac83e6633e859949673ecbc9fe4690, 2026-11-01) escalated
to the full test lane under xdist (1 failed, 59651 passed, 18 skipped, 19m28s) and
failed exactly this node on worker gw8. The test never reached its own body: it failed
inside `async with AcePage() as page` at src/sase/ace/testing/ace_page.py:329 ->
settle_helpers.settle_pilot -> textual pilot `_wait_for_screen` with
`textual.pilot.WaitForScreenTimeout` (the library's 30s default). The node's recorded
call time in that run was 42.47s, versus 2.29s when run alone.

Controls on the unchanged tree: the whole file passed serially right afterwards
(`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ace/tui/test_plugins_browser_pane_update.py`, 9
passed in 28.93s). Fail rate so far: 1/1 under the loaded full lane, 0/1 serial.

Same failure signature (WaitForScreenTimeout under the loaded full lane, passes in
isolation) as the node-specific beads sase-18u and sase-1pq, which suggests a shared
cause in AcePage startup or settle under host load; none of those beads has isolated a
root cause. Sibling plugins-pane update tests in this same file were also reported
failing under load in closed bead sase-154 (a different, tighter wait_for failure).
Investigate why the pilot cannot settle within 30s under load without just raising the
timeout.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: sase tool run check (escalated full xdist lane); serial control: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/ace/tui/test_plugins_browser_pane_update.py

issue.creation_reason: Surfaced as the only failure of a full-lane sase tool run check on an unrelated test-file split; the node passes serially on the same tree and no existing bead covers this node.
